title: Excalibur
dek: The sword of Arthurian legend, whose earliest names predate the stone-in-the-anvil story by centuries and whose supposed grave was found at Glastonbury in 1191.

facts.provenance: Named in Culhwch and Olwen (c. 1100) as Caledfwlch; Latinised by Geoffrey of Monmouth (1136).
facts.whereabouts: Never recovered. The 1191 Glastonbury exhumation produced a cross, not a blade.

prose.label: Names and stories
prose.body: Welsh tradition gives Caledfwlch; French romance splits sword-from-stone and lake-gift traditions. Malory fused them for English readers.
